questions.question: What is the navigation path to access the Engineering license overview dashboard in the Software Asset Workspace?

options.text: Software asset > License Management > Engineering overview
Software asset > Software Asset Workspace > Software asset analytics > Engineering license overview
Software Asset Workspace > Reports > Engineering licenses

explanation.correct: The Engineering license overview dashboard is accessed by navigating to Software asset > Software Asset Workspace > Software asset analytics > Engineering license overview. This dashboard displays reports on normalized products and publishers for engineering applications.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This path does not exist in the Software Asset Workspace navigation.
There is no 'Engineering' top-level module; engineering licenses are managed within Software Asset Workspace.
The Engineering license overview is under Software asset analytics, not under Reports.

source.excerpt: You can access the Engineering license overview dashboard by navigating to Software asset > Software Asset Workspace > Software asset analytics > Engineering license overview.

questions.question: Which metrics are displayed in the Engineering license overview dashboard? (Choose two.)

options.text: Top denied products and Top denied users

explanation.correct: The Engineering license overview dashboard displays Total spend (total cost of all entitlements), Potential savings (cost saved if removal candidates are reclaimed), Top denied products (products denied due to peak concurrent usage), and Top denied users (users denied licenses to products).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Hardware asset utilization is tracked in Hardware Asset Management, not in the Engineering license dashboard which focuses on software licenses.
Contract expiration dates are managed in contract management modules, not in the Engineering license overview dashboard.

source.excerpt: Total spend: Total cost of all entitlements for all products. Potential savings: Cost saved if removal candidates are reclaimed. Top denied products: Top products that are denied to users as these products have reached their peak concurrent usage.

questions.question: In the Engineering license overview dashboard, what does the User session summary report display?

options.text: Number of active user accounts in the system
Duration of time spent by users (idle vs active) on products
User login frequency over the past year
Total number of sessions per user per product

explanation.correct: The User session summary report shows the duration of time spent by users (idle vs active) on products. Only the top 5 users with more idle duration appear on the report. Idle is calculated from the Total idle duration column and Active from the Total session duration column.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The User session summary focuses on product usage duration, not on counting active user accounts.
Login frequency is not tracked in this report; it specifically tracks idle vs active duration on products.
While session data is involved, the report specifically compares idle vs active duration rather than counting total sessions.

source.excerpt: User session summary: Duration of time spent by users (idle vs active) on products. Only the top 5 users with more idle duration appear on the report.

questions.question: Which is NOT a main feature area of the Software Asset Management application?

explanation.correct: Hardware lifecycle management is NOT a feature of Software Asset Management. SAM focuses on software assets including Dashboards, Licensing, Discovery and normalization, Reconciliation, Optimization, and Downgrade Rights. Hardware assets are managed through Hardware Asset Management (HAM).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Discovery and normalization is a core SAM feature that identifies installed software and normalizes discovered products against the ServiceNow repository.
Reconciliation is a main SAM feature that calculates compliance status by comparing discovered software against entitlements.
Downgrade Rights is a SAM feature that manages the process of using rights for earlier software versions while having acquired rights to the latest version.

source.excerpt: Software Asset Management functionality consists of these main features: Dashboards, Licensing, Discovery and normalization, Reconciliation, Optimization, Downgrade Rights.

questions.question: Which dashboards are available in the Software Asset Management application? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: SAM includes Software Asset Analytics (Overview, License Summary, Compliance Summary, Removal Summary), Normalization and Content Service (Normalization trend charts), and Software Publisher Analytics (Citrix, IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, VMware - requires publisher pack add-on).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Hardware Utilization is part of Hardware Asset Management, not Software Asset Management.
Network Discovery is part of the Discovery application, not a SAM dashboard.

source.excerpt: Dashboards: Software Asset Analytics: Overview, License Summary, Compliance Summary, and Removal Summary. Normalization and Content Service: Normalization trend charts. Software Publisher Analytics: Citrix, IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, and VMware.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Oracle publisher overview in Software Asset Workspace are true?
a) True-up cost shows the cost to be compliant based on the average price of rights in Oracle software entitlements.
b) The overview displays unlicensed installations, subscriptions, and client access records.
c) License types shown include BYOL and License Included for cloud platforms.
d) The Oracle overview is updated weekly by a scheduled job.

explanation.correct: Statements a, b, and c are true. Statement d is false because results are updated whenever a new reconciliation result is available, not weekly by a scheduled job.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement d is false - updates occur with each reconciliation result, not weekly.
Statement a is true - True-up cost is based on average price of rights in Oracle entitlements.
Statement b is also true - the overview displays unlicensed installations, subscriptions, and client access records.

source.excerpt: True-up cost: Cost to be compliant based on the average price of rights in your Oracle software entitlements. Results are updated whenever a new reconciliation result is available.

questions.question: An administrator wants to view how many Oracle software installations are currently unlicensed. Which section of the Oracle publisher overview should they access?

explanation.correct: The Unlicensed entities section displays a summary including Unlicensed installs (total number of unlicensed Oracle software installations), Installs requiring action, Unlicensed subscriptions, Unlicensed client access, and Unlicensed options. Selecting the number allows viewing the complete list.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Progress indicators show compliance progress including Ignored installs, Removal candidates, and Invalid configurations - not unlicensed installations.
License types on cloud platforms shows BYOL vs License Included distributions for Azure and AWS, not unlicensed counts.
True-up cost shows the cost to become compliant, not the count of unlicensed installations.

source.excerpt: Unlicensed entities: Summary of your unlicensed entities. This summary includes: Unlicensed installs: Total number of unlicensed Oracle software installations.

questions.question: What table stores the engineering application products and publishers that appear in the Engineering license overview dashboard filter?

explanation.correct: Only products and publishers that belong to engineering applications and are listed in the Engineering Application License [samp_eng_app_license] table appear in the filter. If no product or publisher is selected, cumulative data for all engineering applications appears.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This table name does not match the documented table for engineering application license filtering.
Software Installation [alm_software_install] stores software installation records generally, not specifically for engineering application filter criteria.
Product Result [samp_product_result] is used for the Total spend metric, not for the filter dropdown population.

source.excerpt: Only products and publishers that belong to engineering applications and are listed in the Engineering Application License [samp_eng_app_license] table appear in the filter.

questions.question: Which plugin must be activated to access the Software Asset Workspace instead of the classic Software Asset Management interface?

explanation.correct: The Software Asset Workspace plugin (com.sn_sam_workspace) must be activated to access the new workspace experience. After activation, the classic Software Asset Management interface menus are hidden for features moved to the workspace.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Professional plugin provides core SAM functionality but does not enable the Workspace interface.
This is the foundation plugin, not the workspace plugin.
This relates to discovery, not the Software Asset Workspace interface.

source.excerpt: The Software Asset Management application is available with activation of the Software Asset Workspace plugin (com.sn_sam_workspace). After the Workspace plugin is activated, you cannot revert to the classic Software Asset Management application.

questions.question: Which features are part of the Software Asset Management application's core functionality? (Choose three.)

options.text: Discovery and normalization of installed software

explanation.correct: The SAM application's core functionality includes: Discovery and normalization (matching discovered software to a centralized library), Reconciliation (calculating compliance status based on rights used vs purchased), and Optimization/Reclamation (uninstalling unused software and reclaiming rights).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Hardware lifecycle management is part of Hardware Asset Management (HAM), not SAM.
Network monitoring is not a function of Software Asset Management.

source.excerpt: Software Asset Management functionality consists of: Dashboards, Licensing, Discovery and normalization, Reconciliation, Optimization.
